prompt: What is the OrderStatus flow?
response: OrderStatus (models.py:383-403): pending_payment -> confirmed -> pending_restaurant (3-min window) -> preparing -> ready_for_pickup -> pending_delivery_decision (3-min window) -> out_for_delivery -> delivered. Branch: pending_restaurant can -> declined_by_restaurant or restaurant_timeout. pending_delivery_decision can -> restaurant_will_deliver or delivery_decision_timeout. Any active status can -> cancelled. Terminal: delivered, cancelled, declined_by_restaurant, restaurant_timeout, delivery_decision_timeout.

prompt: What is the RideRequestStatus flow?
response: RideRequestStatus (models.py:1248-1256): open -> bidding (when first bid arrives) -> matched (customer accepts bid) -> in_progress (driver starts ride) -> completed. Can also: open/bidding -> cancelled (customer cancels) or -> expired (bidding timeout). Never: in_progress -> cancelled (blocked since Feb 17, 2026).

prompt: How does the rideshare tiered fee work in the backend?
response: Function get_tier_fee(fare) at rideshare_payments.py:36-43: fare <= $35 returns $1, fare <= $70 returns $2, fare > $70 returns $3. Applied to BOTH customer AND driver. Customer pays: fare + tier_fee. Driver receives: fare - tier_fee. Platform earns: tier_fee * 2. Example: $50 fare = $2 fee, customer pays $52, driver gets $48, platform gets $4. Source: rideshare_payments.py:80-95.

prompt: How does the food delivery fee work in the backend?
response: Customer pays: food + tax + $1 service fee + delivery fee + tip. Restaurant pays: $1 platform fee (deducted from payout). Driver receives: delivery fee + 100% of tip ($0 commission). Platform: $1 from customer + $1 from restaurant = $2/order. Delivery fee: base $2.49 + $0.50/mile, min $2.99, max $12.99. Surge capped at 2.0x. Source: order_flow.py:400-409, 424.

prompt: How does the backend start up?
response: FastAPI app created in main_new.py. Startup event (line 1199) calls: init_db() (creates tables), _run_startup_migrations() (38+ ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS statements across 7 tables), start_timeout_scheduler() (background job for order timeouts). Shutdown calls stop_timeout_scheduler(). Run with: uvicorn main_new:app --reload --port 8080. Source: main_new.py:1199-1210.

prompt: How does the CORS middleware work?
response: Production origins: dollor.ai, api.dollor.ai, vibingticket.com, CloudFront CDN. Staging: d3kuu45w6kl8hr.cloudfront.net. Dev: localhost:3000, 5173, 8080. Environment-aware: fails safe to production (no localhost in production). fix_cors_headers middleware (line 152): always sets Vary: Origin, strips allow-credentials if no allow-origin. Also adds 7 security headers: HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-XSS-Protection. Source: main_new.py:96-172.

prompt: How does admin authentication work?
response: admin_auth_middleware (main_new.py:174-228) protects ALL /api/admin/* endpoints by default. Two auth methods: (1) Bearer JWT token with admin role, (2) ADMIN_SECRET_KEY query param. Exempt: /api/admin/login, /api/admin/set-document-status (has own body-based auth). Returns 401 if no valid auth. Defense in depth: individual endpoints can also use Depends(get_current_user). Source: main_new.py:174-228.

prompt: How does rate limiting work?
response: In-memory sliding window rate limiter (main_new.py:232-265). Thread-safe. Auth endpoints: 10 requests per 60 seconds per IP. Registration: 5 requests per 300 seconds per IP. Key: IP address + endpoint type. Falls back to X-Forwarded-For header for load balancers. Applied to all 4 login endpoints. Returns 429 Too Many Requests when exceeded.

prompt: How is the backend deployed to ECS?
response: Build: docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t dollor-api:tag . (Apple Silicon needs amd64 for Fargate). Push: docker tag + push to ECR 134607809447.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/dollor-api:{git-sha}. Register: aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json file://task-def.json. Update: aws ecs update-service --cluster dollor-production --service dollor-api-service --task-definition dollor-api:{revision}. CRITICAL: Task def uses git SHA tag, NOT :latest.

prompt: How does the pricing_config.py fare calculation work?
response: Base rates: BASE_FARE=$2.50, PER_MILE_RATE=$1.15, PER_MINUTE_RATE=$0.18, MINIMUM_FARE=$8.00 (pricing_config.py:18-21). Formula: max(MIN_FARE, BASE_FARE + distance*PER_MILE + duration*PER_MINUTE). Time multipliers: morning 1.15x, evening 1.20x, late night 1.10x, off-peak 0.95x. Distance discounts: 10-25mi 5%, 25-50mi 10%, 50+mi 15%. Demand cap: 0.90x to 1.50x. Note: main_new.py:3239 uses different rates ($1.50/mi, $0.25/min).
